summary: Verified CORS + Bearer auth fix for GitHub Pages deployment. Backend: 11/11 pytest tests pass covering (1) cross-origin Bearer flow through PUBLIC_URL with Origin=github.io returning 200 on /api/auth/me (owner super_admin), /api/dashboard/stats, /api/santri, /api/pembayaran; (2) logout via Bearer deletes MongoDB session and subsequent /me returns 401 (used a disposable TEST_ session, owner token preserved); (3) direct backend (localhost:8001) CORS preflight reflects allow-origin: https://example-user.github.io with allow-credentials: true (not wildcard) — proving middleware config; preview origin also reflected; (4) non-allowed origin https://evil.example.com preflight is NOT reflected (400, no matching allow-origin); (5) 401 for missing/invalid tokens. Frontend regression: /login renders [data-testid=google-login-button]; with session_token cookie + localStorage the dashboard route loads with stat cards (Total Santri, Santri Putra/Putri, Pembayaran Bulan Ini, Tagihan Belum Lunas), sidebar (Data Santri, Pembayaran, Tagihan, Laporan, Master Data, Manajemen Admin, Aktivitas, Pengaturan) and charts. Frontend compiled successfully (webpack). Code integrity confirmed: api.js has withCredentials:false + Bearer interceptor from localStorage('session_token'); AuthCallback.jsx stores session_token to localStorage; AuthContext.jsx logout removes localStorage token; server.py CORSMiddleware uses explicit allow_origins from CORS_ORIGINS env plus allow_origin_regex=https://.*\.github\.io, and /api/auth/logout accepts Bearer header fallback.

issues: Recharts warns 'width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' during initial mount before ResponsiveContainer measures — cosmetic console noise only, charts render correctly after layout settles.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py CORSMiddleware allow_origins filters out '*' correctly, and allow_origin_regex covers github.io subdomains — good.
get_current_user() falls back to Authorization: Bearer when cookie is absent — enables cross-origin flow without third-party cookies.
AuthCallback stores session_token in localStorage — works, but note this is XSS-exfiltrable; acceptable trade-off for GitHub Pages deployment.

Frontend api.js has withCredentials:false globally; same-origin preview relies on the browser sending cookies by default with axios when no CORS is triggered — this is fine but subtle. Consider a comment or a runtime switch based on hostname if future issues arise.
server.py is ~760 lines mixing auth, CRUD for santri/tagihan/pembayaran, PDF, dashboard, export/import — splitting into routers would improve maintainability (not blocking).

rca of the issue: Original bug: browsers blocked credentialed cross-origin auth from https://<user>.github.io because backend returned ACAO:* with Allow-Credentials:true AND cookies are third-party across origins. Fix confirmed working: (a) backend allow_origins now explicit + allow_origin_regex for github.io so preflight reflects specific origin with credentials:true; (b) frontend switched to non-credentialed Bearer header from localStorage, sidestepping the third-party cookie block entirely; (c) backend /api/auth/logout accepts Bearer fallback so logout succeeds cross-origin. All 11 verification tests pass.
